what: First adversarial review of pull request 2 of BRIEF-canon.md (They take their own recoil: the push back from their own moves goes to their source, the endless ocean, not the planet; items 2, 3 and 7: the engine's recoilAbsorbed figures, the planted catcher, the feet carrying only the weights, the momentum ledger in test/powers.js, and the page and README copy). Three lenses: physics (the engine's figures and the README's claims against canon and an independent re-calculation); code and tests (the powers-off identity, mutants of every new path, the ledger, the page's new checks); copy and layout (every changed sentence against the engine and the page as rendered). Reviewed at ba45ba9 (the engine at 87c9dc3 and the page) and 51782b3 (the STATUS commit on top). Each finding was reproduced or refuted by a skeptic with its own script; 10 were confirmed and fixed, 2 refuted (their optional wording applied).

The same holds with own recoil alone.

Decision 3 physics: in the engine's force model the hand force on the object plus arm is (F - RB) u + mB g y-hat. With the power on, the recoil part (F - RB) u goes to the source and the feet carry exactly (mA + mB) g = (body.m + obj.m) g = anc.N(RB), even while he accelerates the object upward. Checked: sinkRatio = (3000 + m_obj) g / Nmax exactly in every throw case. The throw's ground preset with the power on (weights only) is a stated reading that the page explains.

The catch throw's J matches the flight's momentum within 0.04% over 7 dials, 6 objects, 4 distances and 2 surfaces. Every power-on catch has uAfter 0, slide 0 and no toGroundT or toGroundC.

Unchanged with the powers on, compared by hash with main: jump, clap, sprint, Collide (sprint, jump and stomp charges, splat and bounce) and instant growth on concrete and sand at 4 dials and 5 power states. Unbreakable-only results (throw, stomp, punch, pull, shove, wrestle throw, catches, toss, arm) are identical to main except the new additive key weakGround.downTaken. Powers off: 15,541 cases identical (test/powers.js --off-only).
weakGround's switch from ownAnchor(ctx) to ctx.anchor reaches no call with ownRecoil on: the throw and throwPushJ are only called with it off, and the catch and landing pass an explicit override.

Every ocean entry with the powers on is one of canon's cases: recoil, the ground's share it can't bear (stomp blow cap, jump push-off, Collide, partner landing), the growth lift. None comes from their own push into the ground. test/powers.js passes 142/142 (366 ledgers, worst residual 1.3e-9).

Cards and engine comments list canon's momentum cases correctly (own recoil, the air's drag, the ground's share it can't bear, the growth lift, incoming hits and flight not yet modelled). 'It carries almost no energy, since they don't move' is right for a source that takes momentum without motion.

findings.title: Arm-wrestle pin: recoilAbsorbed.J is the forearms' net momentum, not the winner's push back; the loser's push back is missing and the ledger nets the two
findings.location: rex-strength-lab/src/engine.js armWrestle (ownPin, Jpin, out.recoilAbsorbed ~L1822-1825); test/powers.js section 6 arm-pin ledger (~L846-860)
findings.evidence: The engine's own pin model is pushApart({F: Aw, mA: M, RA: Infinity, mB: M, RB: Pl}). The winner's push on the forearms is Aw for the whole swing, so his push back is Aw*t. The loser's arm resists with Pl, and its push back (Pl*t, downward) acts on the loser. Jpin = sqrt(E^2+2EMc^2)/c = pB = (Aw-Pl)*t is only the net of the two. Script (Rex at 100 short tons, Ollie as a what-if, powers on, concrete): Ollie at 0.5x: recoilAbsorbed.J 3,430 kg m/s; winner's push back Aw*t 6,861; loser's Pl*t 3,430. At 0.9x: 1,534 vs 15,340 (loser 13,810). At 0.99x: 485 vs 48,510 (loser 48,030). The engine header documents recoilAbsorbed as the push back on the person who takes it (and the pin as 'the swing's push back goes to his source'), so the figure is up to 100x too small. The ledger books own(aw.recoilAbsorbed) against pE(aw.pin.E, aw.pin.M), the same formula, under a comment 'the swing's push back on the winner (up)'. It closes by construction and would fail the correct Aw*t. The ground's slam (toGround.J = pB) is right when both have the power on, and the page doesn't show Jpin. The figure matters for pull request 4, where the canon says each one's own push back is absorbed.
findings.expected: Q12/Q15: in arm wrestling each one's own push back goes to his own source. The winner's source should take Aw*t upward, and the loser's source Pl*t downward when he has the power on. When he doesn't (possible through the engine API, not the page), Pl*t goes into the ground through the loser during the swing and partly cancels a quick slam. The ocean's net, (Aw-Pl)*t upward, is unchanged.
findings.fix: Report the winner's push back as Aw*t (the integral of his force over the swing in real mode) in recoilAbsorbed. Report the loser's resisting push back separately, for example recoilAbsorbedL { J: Pl*t, thetaDeg: 90 }, only with the loser's power on. Book both in the ledger as two 'ocean:recoil' entries. Or, if the netting is meant, relabel the field and its comments as 'the net of both sides' push backs (the slam's momentum)' and add a check that names the split.

verdict.reasoning: The numbers reproduce: in comic mode recoilAbsorbed.J for the pin is the forearms' net momentum (Aw-Pl)*t, not the winner's own push back Aw*t. That is still not a defect in this pull request. (1) Canon says they share one infinite source, and the engine header defines recoilAbsorbed as 'the momentum their source takes back'. With both powers on, the winner's push back (Aw*t, up) and the loser's (Pl*t, down) both go into that one source, so the source's net take is exactly (Aw-Pl)*t = Jpin. The ground gets only the slam (toGround.J = pB). Both totals are correct. (2) The page can't give the two different recoil settings: ctxOllie() is Object.assign(ctx(), {F, body, anchor}), so Ollie always inherits Rex's ownRecoil. The ledger's states also set both alike. The mixed case, where the split would change the ground's figure, can only be reached through the engine API. (3) The brief puts the loser's press, 'each one's own push back ... no longer loads the table through his elbow pad and peg', in item 4 (pull request 4). The engine comment says so: 'The presses through the elbow pads and pegs ... are item 4 ... unchanged here'. (4) The page never shows Jpin. It only says 'The swing's push back goes into W's source', which is true. The ledger's 'ocean:recoil' bucket is right for the net, because both parts are own recoil. The only weakness is wording: the engine comment and the ledger comment call the net 'the swing's push back on the winner'. Pull request 4 should tidy that when it splits the presses. It is not a wrong figure or a broken test.

findings.title: A planted catcher's slam is booked and described as his own push back, though about 40% of the momentum hits his chest after his arms stop pushing
findings.location: rex-strength-lab/src/engine.js CATCHGAME.leg recoilAbsorbedC (~L3334-3336) and catchIt uAfter; src/app.html bayCatch item (~L2937); test/powers.js section 6 catch stop booked as 'ocean:recoil'
findings.evidence: Catch, bus 10 m apart, thrown hard, default dial, powers on (the README's own example). The page says: 'stopping it is Ollie’s own push, so its push back (140,000 kg·m/s, the bus’s momentum) goes into their source … so it slams into him'. My independent split: the arrival momentum is m v = 9,525 x 14.289 = 136,100. First contact gives v1 = 14.094 m/s with the hands (mS = 9,657 kg). His arms, at Fcap 889,644 N over d = 0.9144 m, take it from 14.094 to vSlam 5.691 m/s (the engine agrees): an impulse of about 81,100 (plus 1,100 from gravity). The remaining mS*vSlam = 55,000 kg m/s (40%) reaches his chest as a hit, with no push of his. recoilAbsorbedC.J = 136,100 books all of it as his own recoil, and the ledger files it under 'ocean:recoil'. The canon (CLAUDE.md, rulings of 14 Oct) lists 'a caught object' among incoming hits (Never knocked back). Slams arise newly in this pull request because the catcher is planted.
findings.expected: The arms' stop is his own push back (They take their own recoil, as the brief reads Q5). The slam into his chest is an incoming hit. Canon absorbs it too ('a catch is absorbed'), but under the incoming-hits case, not as his own push. The page shouldn't call the whole 140,000 kg·m/s his own push's push back.
findings.fix: Either split the figure: recoilAbsorbedC for the arms' stop, mS(v1 - vSlam) plus the first-contact share, and a separate slam figure (mS*vSlam, an incoming hit) for pull request 4's Never knocked back to take over, with the ledger booking it under its own label. Or keep one figure and reword the page and README decision 4: '…his arms stop X; the rest slams into his chest (Y), and a catch is absorbed whole (canon)'. State in the README that the slam is taken back under 'a catch is absorbed' until Never knocked back exists.

verdict.reasoning: The split reproduces. Bus, 10 m apart, thrown hard, default dial, powers on: the result is 'slams'. The arms take F*t = 82,200 kg m/s (81,100 plus 1,100 from gravity). The chest takes mS*vSlam = 55,000 kg m/s, about 40%. recoilAbsorbedC.J = 136,101, all of it. That is a recorded, justified decision, not a defect. Canon (rulings of 14 Oct): 'A catch is absorbed (he is never carried off, and nothing goes into the ground) unless he chooses otherwise.' The whole momentum going to the source matches that. The bucket follows the brief's stated reading. Q5's answer is 'the catcher's stop is his own push back (item 2)', and Q2's answer is 'what's left on the page is catches, absorbed through item 2'. 'Unless he chooses otherwise' is mapped to turning They take their own recoil off. The finding's alternative split (arms = own recoil, chest = incoming hit) is not more canonical either. Canon's incoming-hit list names 'a caught object' as a whole, so on that reading even the arms' stop is an incoming hit. Both readings absorb all of it. The README states it (decision 4: 'his stop goes to the endless ocean in every outcome where the object reaches him ... a catch his slide used to share can become a slam'). So does the engine comment ('what his arms couldn't stop slams into him and his source takes that too'). The page states the slam plainly in the line above ('Ollie can't stop it with his arms ... hits him at 5.69 m/s'). The momentum figure is labelled correctly as 'the bus's momentum'. The totals, the outcome and the 'nothing into the ground' claim are all right in every reachable state.

findings.title: The stomp's 'upper bound' caveat is limited to Bolted with the power off, but on friction footing with the power off the standing foot unloads in the same way
findings.location: rex-strength-lab/README.md decision 5 and Known limits ('bolted with the power off, the bolts' upward pull partly cancels it'); src/app.html bayStomp items (~L1771-1773: caveat only when r.bolted)
findings.evidence: Powers off, friction footing, concrete. At 20,000 kg-force on the dial: F 24,950 N < mA g 27,630 N, so pA = 0 (his weight holds him down) and pB = 2,890 kg m/s. During the push his standing foot unloads by the whole 2,890 kg m/s, the same cancellation the bolted case describes. Yet the page shows 2.37 mm/s at 5 m with no caveat (the item exists only for r.bolted). At the default dial, pB 6,009 and pA 4,542, so the standing foot unloads by 1,467 (24% of the blow) before he lifts off. The ledger itself books that unloading for these states ('ground:recoil' (0, pB - pA), 'his standing foot unloads'). The page text is unchanged from main, but this pull request's new README sentence says the caveat stays only for Bolted.
findings.expected: With They take their own recoil off, the foot's blow alone is an upper bound whether the push back goes through the bolts or through the standing foot (fully so when his weight holds him down). The caveat goes only with the power on, where the source holds him and the standing foot's load doesn't change.
findings.fix: Extend the caveat to friction footing with the power off: in README decision 5 and Known limits ('with the power off, bolted or standing, the push back through the bolts or the standing foot partly cancels it'), and in the stomp's items (an item for !r.bolted && !sa that says the standing foot unloads by the push not spent lifting him).

verdict.reasoning: This reproduces, and the pull request introduced the asymmetry. Powers off on concrete at a 20,000 kg-force dial, the stomp on friction footing and the stomp bolted are physically identical: F 24,951 N < mA g 27,625 N, so pA = 0 and pB = 2,890 kg m/s in both. During the push, the standing foot unloads by the whole pB in both cases. That is exactly the upward pull the bolted caveat describes. The engine gives both the same blow and the same shaking: 2.374 mm/s at 5 m. Yet the page now tells only the bolted reader that the shaking is an upper bound. The friction text is unchanged and has no caveat ('Here his weight holds him down and the foot takes all of the energy.'). On main, neither powers-off case carried the caveat. Main's own caveat was about the standing foot ('the upward pull through his standing foot comes at almost the same moment and partly cancels it'). This pull request moved the caveat to Bolted with the power off only. Its new README text (decision 5: 'it stays for Bolted with the power off'; Known limits: 'A stomp's foot blow ... reaches the ground whole and nothing cancels it (bolted with the power off, the bolts' upward pull partly cancels it ...)') leaves out the standing-foot case. That case is the same physics, and the test's own ledger books it ('ground:recoil' (0, pB - pA), 'his standing foot unloads'). At the default dial on friction, the foot still unloads by pB - pA = 1,467 kg m/s, about a quarter of the foot's 6,009, before he hops. The shaking drives the stomp's effort goal, its courtesy ceiling and its presets, so the same number is labelled an upper bound in one case and not in the other.

findings.title: README 'What moved' says the plaster reach and presets don't move for objects up to a pickup, but they do for level throws on sand and for the ground preset
findings.location: rex-strength-lab/README.md, section 'Their own recoil goes to their source', What moved, first bullet
findings.evidence: Engine runs of main against the branch, all-out, powers on, RESTRAINT.reach plaster at 5 m. Car thrown level on sand: 10^7 kg dial 109 -> 93.3 m; 10^8 kg 264 -> 234 m; 10^9 kg 640 -> 572 m. Pickup level on sand: 10^7 135 -> 111 m; 10^9 791 -> 706 m. His push, not the landing, set these (plasterReach takes the larger source). The break-the-ground preset also moves for a car and a pickup at 45 degrees at a 10^9 kg dial on concrete: 650,200 kg-force -> never. The next bullet reports that one, so the first bullet contradicts it. The courtesy ceilings for these objects are unchanged (checked on concrete, gravel and sand at 10^9 kg).
findings.expected: The claim should match the runs: for objects up to a pickup the courtesy ceiling and the shaking presets don't move, but the all-out plaster reach falls for level throws on sand at high dials, and the break-the-ground preset moves as the next bullet says.
findings.fix: Reword the bullet. For example: 'For objects up to a pickup the courtesy ceiling and the rattle and plaster presets don't move; the all-out plaster reach of a level throw on sand falls where his push set it (a car at a 10^9 kg dial: 640 to 572 m), and the break-the-ground preset changes as below.'

verdict.reasoning: This reproduces in the engine and on the page. The README's 'What moved' first bullet says: 'For objects up to a pickup the plaster reach, the courtesy ceiling and the presets don't move, as the brief expected.' For all-out level throws on sand, the plaster reach falls, because his push back on the sand, now absorbed, used to set it. The page's 'Where each hazard starts' row for a car thrown level on sand at a 10^9 kg dial reads 'now out to 640 m' on main and 'now out to 572 m' on the branch. The break-the-ground preset also moves for a car and a pickup at 45 degrees at a 10^9 kg dial on concrete: 650,200 kg-force becomes never. The README's second bullet reports that change, so the first bullet contradicts it. The courtesy ceilings and the rattle, plaster, windows and houses presets for these objects are unchanged in every case checked: sand, concrete and gravel at 0 degrees, and concrete at 45 degrees. The physics change is correct and the claim about it is wrong: an inaccurate statement in the record the owner reads.
